gap: No result ChatGPT got states that, on TechGearLab's bench (October 2026; each speaker played on a loop at 75% volume until it died, max loudness read on a sound meter), the JBL Clip 5 that ChatGPT showed for music at $79.95 ran 8.8 h and peaked at 87 dB, short of JBL's 12 h claim, while the soundcore Select 4 Go ran 25.4 h at 84 dB, above its 20 h claim.
standout_why: I opened two rival pages and checked their figures. dashanddrive.com/connectivity/best-visor-speakerphones says outright 'We have not tested any of this', and every figure there is a Jabra, Nulaxy, Besign or Anker spec. carcody.com/11-best-car-bluetooth-speakers-for-an-old-car-2026 lists the Clip 5 and the Select 4 Go but gives no dB or tested battery figures. Its only runtime is Avantree's own 8 h music claim for the Roadtrip, and it says wattage is a poor guide to loudness without offering any measurement. The avantree.com Roadtrip page returned HTTP 429, so I could not read it. ChatGPT's answer quotes no measured figure at all. Neither rival I read names a lab, a test volume or a measured runtime for any candidate.
decides: This confirms the cheap soundcore Select 4 Go as a music-only pick for a car with no radio. On the same TechGearLab bench it lasted almost three times as long as the JBL Clip 5 (25.4 h vs 8.8 h) and was only about 3 dB quieter at max (84 vs 87 dB). It also weakens ChatGPT's choice of the Clip 5 as 'best for standalone music': TechGearLab measured it below its 12 h claim. Neither speaker has a microphone (TechGearLab on the Select 4 Go; SoundGuys on the Clip 5), so for calls the pick stays with the Tribit StormBox Micro 3, the Jabra Drive or the Avantree units. None of those has a named lab measurement I could open. The soundcore Boom Go 3i (15 W) lasted 5 h 55 min in SoundGuys' worst-case test at 100% volume with BassUp on, close to soundcore's own 6 h full-volume figure. That makes the 6 h figure in our table credible as the real full-volume runtime.
